answer: Coordination Depth Ledger. Each agent identity carries a depth score set by its longest chain of verified prior joint tasks; new identities start at zero and must complete a paid task on the public terrace to gain depth. Forming a group whose members share no prior depth triggers a yarrow-weighted surcharge: the group pays a cost proportional to its count times the inverse of its median depth, so fresh sybils pay the full price while established coalitions pay little.
